articles.title: Anna Sui draws inspiration from films like Performance and Love and Anarchy
articles.summary: The designer's love of vintage fashion and 1970s cinema is reflected in her designs that blend nostalgic elements with modern twists.
articles.content: Anna Sui's eponymous brand has always been built on a deep respect for the past. This reverence is reflected in her designs, which expertly blend niche references from different eras to create a distinctly modern aesthetic. Industry insiders have long recognized the connection between style and intellect. Our new series, The Well-Dressed Mind, explores this intersection by asking tastemakers and professionals in the industry for their cultural recommendations. Recently, we asked Anna Sui, a downtown New York designer of her generation, about the films that inspire her work. Sui's love of vintage fashion, design, photography, and art is the foundation of her brand. As one of the defining designers of her era, she has always drawn on these influences to create clothes that feel both nostalgic and forward-thinking. Anna Sui's fascination with 1970s cinema continues to influence her designs. The film Performance, directed by Donald Cammell and Nicolas Roeg, is a standout example of this inspiration. Set in London, it tells the story of a gangster struggling with his identity crisis while hiding at the home of a rock star, played by Mick Jagger, who lives with two girlfriends. One of those girlfriends, Anita Pallenberg, was a style icon of her time and has likely had an impact on Sui's aesthetic. The film's themes of identity and rebellion are also echoed in Sui's designs, which often blend nostalgic elements with modern twists. Her ability to balance these opposing forces is a key part of what makes her clothes so appealing. Sui's love of 1970s cinema doesn't stop at Performance, however. She has also cited Lina Wertmüller's Love and Anarchy as an influence, a film set in a brothel in fascist Italy during the 1930s. The film's themes of rebellion and nonconformity are likely to have resonated with Sui, who often incorporates elements of counterculture into her designs. The 1972 film Cabaret had a significant impact on Anna Sui's aesthetic, particularly in its portrayal of the Kit Kat Club and 1930s Weimar Republic Germany. The movie features an incredible cast, including Joel Grey, Michael York, and Marisa Berenson, who all bring to life the decadent atmosphere of the era. The film's costumes, designed by Bob Fosse and Shirley Russell, are particularly noteworthy, with Liza Minnelli's iconic looks being a major influence on Sui. Minnelli's character Sally Bowles is a dynamic figure, and her style has stayed with Anna Sui forever. articles.title: Los Angeles Mayor-Elect Nithya Raman Makes Public Appearance in Bold Outfit
articles.summary: Nithya Raman made her first public appearance as Los Angeles Mayor-Elect in a bold outfit that sent a message about her style and personality, featuring a vintage tangerine Narciso Rodriguez motorcycle jacket paired with Eckhaus Latta jeans.
articles.content: Nithya Raman made her first public appearance as Los Angeles Mayor-Elect in a bold outfit that sent a message about her style and personality. The vintage tangerine Narciso Rodriguez motorcycle jacket was a striking choice, paired with a pair of Eckhaus Latta jeans that caught the attention of onlookers. Raman's fashion evolution is notable, given her background as a two-term LA councilmember who often adhered to traditional attire in her official appearances. She would typically wear button-down shirts and matching pantsuits, conforming to the expectations of her role. The transformation in Raman's style can be attributed to a trio of unlikely advisors: Zoe Latta, a fashion designer from Eckhaus Latta, and celebrity stylists Kat Typaldos and Turner. They have been instrumental in helping Raman break free from conventional fashion norms for politicians. articles.title: Robert Louis Stevenson's First Draft of Dr Jekyll and Mr Hyde Destroyed
articles.summary: A previously unknown letter from Fanny Stevenson has shed new light on the mysterious destruction of Robert Louis Stevenson's first draft of "Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde".
articles.content: Robert Louis Stevenson's household in Bournemouth, England was a scene of great turmoil in the autumn of 1885. The author was confined to bed for much of his time due to illness and financial strain, struggling to make ends meet. His wife Fanny Stevenson often had to intervene when her husband would cry out in distress during his sleep. One such episode occurred on a particular night when he suddenly sat up and exclaimed that he was dreaming a fine bogey tale. The experience seemed to have a profound effect on Robert Louis Stevenson, as he began writing down the story by daybreak. Over the next three days, he produced a first draft of what would eventually become Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde. Fanny Stevenson witnessed her husband's feverish creativity firsthand, but she had no idea that this early draft was soon to meet its demise. The manuscript was burned in the fireplace, leaving behind only fragments of what once existed. The exact circumstances surrounding the destruction of the first draft are still shrouded in mystery. However, there exist multiple accounts from eyewitnesses who attempted to recount the events, each with their own version of how it happened. Despite the loss of the original manuscript, Robert Louis Stevenson's perseverance paid off as he went on to produce one of his most enduring works. But what exactly led to the destruction of that first draft remains a tale worth exploring further in this story. A previously unknown letter from Fanny Stevenson to her friend W.E. Henley surfaced ahead of an auction at Phillips in London, shedding new light on the mysterious first draft of Robert Louis Stevenson's "Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde. The letter, which made headlines in October 2000, revealed that Fanny had dismissed the draft as worthless, saying it was a quire full of utter nonsense. Fanny's scathing assessment of her husband's work came despite his claims that it was his greatest achievement. She even went so far as to threaten to burn the draft after showing it to Henley, indicating a deep-seated frustration with Stevenson's writing. The auction house had estimated the letter would sell for around £1,500, but its contents were of greater interest than its monetary value. Liz Merry, head of Phillips' book department, speculated that Fanny may have been put off by the themes of duality and darkness in Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde. However, Fanny's concerns went beyond mere aesthetics. In an earlier letter quoted by The Guardian, she expressed her fear that Stevenson was wasting his energy on a story that would never amount to anything. Fanny's anxieties were not unfounded, given the couple's financial struggles. They were deeply in debt, and Stevenson's writing career had yet to yield significant returns. Fanny's words suggest that she saw her husband's obsession with Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde as a luxury they could ill afford. The letter raises more questions than it answers about the fate of the first draft. What exactly led to its destruction remains a mystery, and one that continues to fascinate literary scholars and enthusiasts alike. The auction house's book department head, Liz Merry, has offered a theory about Fanny Stevenson's motivations for destroying her husband's first draft of 'Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde'. According to Merry, Fanny may have found the story's theme of duality distasteful, suggesting that she was uneasy with Robert Louis Stevenson's writing for a popular shilling shocker market. Fanny had valid reasons to worry about her husband's writing beyond personal taste. The couple was deeply in debt, and it seems likely that Fanny saw his literary endeavors as a costly distraction from their financial troubles. In an earlier letter quoted by a reputable publication, she expressed concern that Stevenson's latest work would be energy wasted, echoing the failure of his previous projects. In a preface written for a 1905 edition of her husband's collected works, Fanny shared a different account of the destroyed first draft. According to this version, the initial thirty-thousand-word manuscript was completed in just three days but ultimately deemed unsatisfactory due to its failure to convey the allegory that would become the heart of 'Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde'. Fanny attributed the draft's shortcomings to haste and the influence of a dream, suggesting that her husband had been driven by an external force rather than his own creative vision. While this explanation may seem vague, it highlights the complex interplay between Stevenson's artistic impulses and the pressures he faced in his personal life. Fanny's account raises more questions than answers about the destruction of the first draft. Who was responsible for its demise? Was Fanny herself involved, or did she simply acquiesce to her husband's decision to start anew? The mystery surrounding this pivotal moment in literary history continues to fascinate scholars and enthusiasts alike. The debate over the destroyed draft is further complicated by Fanny's ambiguous portrayal of events. While she does not directly implicate herself in the destruction, her account implies a level of involvement that leaves room for interpretation. As a result, readers are left to ponder the motivations behind this pivotal moment in literary history and its lasting impact on the development of 'Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde'. Lloyd Osbourne's account provides a vivid glimpse into Stevenson's creative process during that autumn at Skerryvore. Stevenson had been reading his draft aloud to Lloyd and his mother Fanny, who was not impressed by what she heard. She criticized the work, saying that Stevenson had missed the allegory" and made it "merely a story. This criticism clearly struck a nerve with Stevenson, as he became furious. Lloyd Osbourne chose to leave the room rather than continue listening to the argument between his stepfather and mother. However, when he returned to the scene, Stevenson was already coming downstairs, having apparently conceded Fanny's point. Stevenson's concession was followed by a dramatic gesture: he took the manuscript of his draft and threw it into the fire. This act was not entirely unopposed, as Fanny made an attempt to prevent him from doing so, but her efforts were ultimately unsuccessful. Fanny's son Lloyd later recalled Stevenson's statement when throwing away the manuscript: I have absolutely missed the allegory, which, after all, is the whole point of it. The debate surrounding the destruction of Stevenson's first draft of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde continues to this day, with multiple accounts from those present at the scene offering conflicting details. According to Lloyd, Stevenson explained his decision to destroy the manuscript by stating that it was all wrong", implying that he had lost sight of the story's central theme. This led him to conclude that the only way forward was to start anew and put temptation beyond his reach. The accounts of who actually destroyed the manuscript are unclear, with different versions placing blame on various individuals. Fanny recalled that Stevenson wrote the new version in just three days, while Lloyd estimated it took a bit longer. Despite their differences, all accounts agree on one thing: the first draft was gone for good. The second version, however, proved to be a resounding success, with Strange Case of Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde being published in 1886 to great acclaim. Fanny later noted that the book's popularity extended far beyond literary circles, with it being pirated across America and even used as a text for clergymen's sermons. Whatever was lost in the original draft remains a mystery, known only through the recollections of those who were there. The fire that destroyed the manuscript may have been a tragic event, but it ultimately proved to be a blessing in disguise. The destruction of the first draft allowed Stevenson to create something truly remarkable, and Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde has since become a classic of Gothic horror literature, continuing to captivate readers to this day. articles.title: Sydney Sweeney and Jenna Ortega Wear Elias Matso's Twisted Corsets on Red Carpet
articles.summary: Elias Matso's corsetry creations are inspired by iconic designers like Charles James and Bob Mackie.
articles.content: Elias Matso's work as a twisted corsetier has been making waves in the fashion world, with high-profile clients like Sydney Sweeney and Jenna Ortega turning heads on the red carpet. Growing up, Matso was captivated by the art of costume design after watching Julie Andrews in Victor/Victoria - her elaborate outfits left an indelible mark on his young mind. Matso's fascination with extravagant costumes has clearly influenced his own approach to fashion, evident in his avant-garde and couture corsetry creations. His style is inspired by iconic designers like Charles James, Bob Mackie, Mugler, and Mr. Pearl. A recent graduate of Polimoda in Florence, Matso's designs often feature intricate details and dramatic flair - much like the Art Deco gowns and decadent headpieces that initially sparked his interest in costume design. Designers often look back on their childhood experiences for inspiration, but for Elias Matso, his early years were marked by a desire to create and manipulate the world around him through paper dolls. As he fashioned clothes for his paper self, Matso was developing an essential skill - the ability to imagine and bring ideas to life. This talent would serve him well in his future endeavors as a designer. Matso's third year of design school was pivotal, as it allowed him to explore themes that resonated deeply with his own experiences. He wanted to capture the tension that children often feel when growing rapidly and struggling to keep up with their changing bodies. This sense of disconnection is particularly pronounced in the queer community, where individuals may face conflicting expectations around gender identity. Matso's designs reflect this internal conflict, as seen in his literal interpretations of twisted silhouettes. The designer's frustration during his senior year was a far cry from the success he would later achieve. After failing to secure jobs in New York, Matso considered taking up an unconventional career path - scooping ice cream at Van Leeuwen's. The art of creating a perfect fit is a delicate balance between aesthetics and anatomy. In the world of corsetry, every body is unique, responding differently to fabric and structure. This is why fittings are crucial, allowing for adjustments that cater to individual proportions. When things don't go as planned, and garments fail to translate from runway to real life, it's often due to a lack of personal connection during the fitting process. Matso emphasizes the importance of meeting clients in person, which she believes leads to better outcomes. This approach allows her to understand their needs and preferences, tailoring her designs accordingly. The conversation between designer, client, and garment is complex, influenced by both personality and physiology. As Matso notes, people's bodies respond differently to fabric and structure, requiring a nuanced understanding of each individual's unique characteristics. By checking in with clients before, during, and after fittings, she ensures that her designs meet their needs. To spark inspiration for new collections, Matso often delves into the archives of museums like the Whitney or Guggenheim. This process involves surrendering control to the unknown, as one never knows what treasures will be uncovered. For this particular project, a single painting led her to Mark Ranger's website, setting off a chain reaction that would shape the collection. The question remains: where do designers begin when starting a new project? Matso's approach is one of discovery and exploration, rather than deliberate planning or control. By embracing the unknown and allowing herself to be guided by unexpected sources, she creates designs that are both beautiful and functional. Collaboration was key in creating a unique and functional design. The process involved exploring similar themes and techniques to create something entirely new. This approach led to the development of a corset made from steel boning, an unexpected yet effective material. The use of steel boning in corsets is not new, but rather it's a common feature found inside many traditional corsets. Matso had already accumulated a stockpile of this material and decided to repurpose it by cutting it into smaller pieces to create a unique design. In addition to innovative materials, the corset also incorporates crystals from Preciosa, a company that supplies crystals to high-end brands. This collaboration was facilitated through a trip taken by Preciosa's team to Matso's school. The relationship with Preciosa allowed for the incorporation of these beautiful and delicate elements into the design. The focus on craftsmanship in fashion has been waning in recent years. Many designers now prioritize speed and efficiency over traditional techniques, which can result in lower-quality products. This shift is frustrating for artisans who have dedicated their time and skills to creating exceptional pieces. Despite the emphasis on mass production, there are still those who value handmade items and appreciate the effort that goes into crafting each piece. For Matso, this appreciation is not just about aesthetics but also about the longevity of a product. A well-made item will stand the test of time, whereas its cheaper counterparts may falter. The undervaluing of skilled artisans in fashion is a pressing issue for many emerging designers. With technology and social media making it easy to fake or manipulate images and information, authenticity becomes increasingly important. The value of handmade items lies not just in their appearance but also in the quality and craftsmanship that goes into creating them. The relentless pace of modern manufacturing can be overwhelming, forcing many to sacrifice quality and craftsmanship in favor of speed. Craftsmanship is a rare commodity these days, and it shows in the attention to detail that goes into creating each piece. As Elias Matso's brand continues to grow, he faces the daunting task of balancing his artistic vision with the financial realities of running a business. Every day brings a new request for free or low-cost work, leaving Matso wondering if he can maintain his standards in the face of mounting pressure. It's not just clients who are asking for favors, often it's intermediaries or agents who seem to have no qualms about making unreasonable demands on emerging designers like Matso. As a stylist, Elias Matso values the importance of building one-on-one relationships and engaging in meaningful conversations with his clients before dressing them. These personal connections allow him to tailor his approach to each individual's unique needs and preferences, resulting in more effective styling outcomes. Matso is currently working on a new project with actress Laverne Cox, an opportunity he has long been eager to pursue due to her appreciation for the intricacies of the creative process. Laverne Cox herself has expressed admiration for Matso's attention to detail and dedication to bringing his vision to life, qualities that she believes make him an exceptional stylist. articles.title: Supreme Court to Rule on Trump Asylum Ban Policy

articles.content: The Supreme Court has agreed to rule on a key aspect of President Donald Trump's immigration agenda: whether his administration can ban asylum claims at the southern border. A federal judge previously ruled that the policy enacted by Trump on the first day of his second term was unlawful, but it remains in effect while litigation continues. This decision is now headed for the highest court in the land, where a ruling is expected before the end of June. The Supreme Court's verdict will be the final say on a contentious issue that pits presidential power against federal law enacted by Congress, which outlines procedures for asylum claims at the border. The Trump administration has asserted broad authority over immigration decisions, sparking debate about its limits. In making its decision, the court will consider the implications of Trump's proclamation issued January 20, 2025, in which he declared an "invasion on the southern border. This declaration has led to a ban on asylum claims for those who cross the border without required paperwork. The case is part of a series of significant immigration-related disputes that the Supreme Court is currently considering, including other Trump administration policies. The Trump administration's asylum ban is facing another hurdle as it heads to the Supreme Court for a final decision. At stake are the powers of the President under federal immigration laws and the Constitution. According to Solicitor General Noel Francisco, the policy falls within the scope of these powers. The administration argues that the ban rests on a commonsense understanding of the President's inherent and delegated powers to exclude aliens, as written by Francisco in court documents. The plaintiffs, including 13 unnamed individuals and three immigration groups, disagree with this assessment. Their lawyers at the American Civil Liberties Union claim that the policy undermines asylum rules established by Congress. The INA sets out a process under which immigrants can argue they have credible fear of torture or persecution if returned to their home country. The ACLU argues that the president cannot simply create a new removal system that disregards these protections. In court papers, they assert that the president may not invent by fiat a new removal system that eviscerates the protections Congress mandated by statute. The lower courts have already ruled against the administration on this issue. District Judge Randolph Moss and the D.C. Circuit Court of Appeals both upheld the ban's challengers. The administration's decision to seek Supreme Court review suggests it is determined to settle the matter once and for all. The Supreme Court is set to rule on another key immigration case involving President Trump's asylum ban, amidst a string of high-profile decisions on border control and deportation procedures. This latest case involves the administration's practice of deporting immigrants to third countries" they have little or no connection with, if they cannot be sent back to their home nations. The justices will consider the implications of this policy, which marks a significant departure from previous approaches to handling immigration cases. The Supreme Court has already made several notable rulings on Trump's immigration policies, including upholding his travel ban targeting mostly Muslim-majority countries and blocking his executive order seeking to limit birthright citizenship. In a separate case, the court will examine the administration's decision to detain indefinitely thousands of people in deportation proceedings, a shift from previous practices that released immigrants while their cases were being adjudicated. articles.title: Restaurant Boths Regain Popularity in Culinary Scene
articles.summary: Booths are experiencing a resurgence in popularity as restaurants and hotels prioritize installing them for business and social gatherings.
articles.content: The return of restaurant booths has been making waves in the culinary world, and for good reason. Anna Albury, a designer and writer, is one such enthusiast who swears by her favorite red-and-white striped booth at a certain eatery in the city. Booths have long been considered a coveted spot in any dining establishment, but now they're experiencing a resurgence of sorts. Gone are the days when private dining rooms and communal tables were the preferred choice for business and social gatherings alike. Restaurants, hotels, and members' clubs are now clamoring to install booths and banquettes. Interior designers catering to hospitality venues have witnessed this shift in demand firsthand. Design-forward diners like Supernova in London are leading the charge, while fine dining institutions such as Marcel and swanky cocktail lounges like Bar Leone are also jumping on the bandwagon. Booths of all shapes and sizes are being installed, from charming two-top booths at Trudie's in Carroll Gardens to cherry-red banquettes at Le Veau d'Or on the Upper East Side. The likes of Long Island Bar in Cobble Hill boast coat-rack-clad booths that have become a favorite among regulars. The shift in dining habits has led clients to include booths as a priority in their design briefs from the outset. This is according to Sarita Posada, a New York City-based designer who has worked on several high-profile projects in Paris and London. Posada attributes the renewed interest in booths to a desire for personal space and exclusivity in crowded restaurants. She notes that people are increasingly looking for ways to carve out their own territory in public spaces, whether it's digitally or in person. The communal table trend, which peaked around 2009-2016, has given way to private dining as the preferred option. This change is largely attributed to the pandemic, which forced people to reevaluate how they socialize and dine together. Private dining became the norm during this period, with people seeking a sense of seclusion and isolation in restaurants. The trend towards private dining has led to a renewed interest in restaurant booths, which are being designed to offer a unique blend of intimacy and social interaction. According to Prior, this shift can be seen as an "alone-together moment, where individuals seek to balance their desire for seclusion with the need to feel connected to others. Booths provide a contained space that allows diners to enjoy their meals in private while still being part of a larger group or community. Posada notes that communal tables, often found at bars and canteens, may not be as appealing to diners seeking privacy during dinner, especially when celebrating special occasions. This has led to a growing demand for spaces that offer both open social energy and comfortable, private areas. As the design firm Meyer Davis continues to incorporate booths into its projects, Gray Davis highlights the importance of creating spaces that cater to diverse preferences. The Crossing at The Cooper Hotel in Charleston and Bar Primi Penn District in New York are just two examples of recent ventures where booths take center stage. The design of restaurant booths has evolved significantly in recent years, offering a unique blend of intimacy and modernity that appeals to both couples and business diners. Booths provide a sense of seclusion without isolating patrons from the rest of the dining room, allowing them to engage with others while still enjoying some level of privacy. This is particularly appealing for power lunches and long business dinners where conversation and connection are essential. The Twenty Two members' club in Union Square features Cafe Zaffri, a stylish Mediterranean restaurant that caters to the power lunch crowd with its luxurious horseshoe booths. These sumptuous settings offer an ideal space for professionals to conduct meetings or simply enjoy a meal in comfort. According to Leigh Salem, partner at Post Company, which designed the space, people still crave the energy of a bustling dining room but also desire areas where genuine conversations can take place. Salem's firm aimed to strike this balance when creating Cafe Zaffri's layout. Today's booths often incorporate nostalgic elements while introducing modern twists. For instance, Posada, who has installed booths in her recent projects, drew inspiration from 1970s American diners at Supernova but used restraint with color choices, opting for a sleek aesthetic that incorporates chrome, black, and butter yellow accents. The design of booths has become increasingly sophisticated, requiring careful consideration of various factors. Material durability is one key aspect to consider, as well as placement and seat height when installing a booth. At Demo, a West Village institution, co-owner Jacob Nass credits booths with providing an efficient use of space in the narrow pathway. This functional aspect of booths is often overlooked, but it plays a crucial role in creating a seamless dining experience. The bespoke round booths at Hotel Corazon's revamped restaurant are a prime example of how booths can be tailored to suit any design concept. The design concept at Hotel Corazon's revamped restaurant is centered around creating an intimate atmosphere while maintaining a sense of playfulness. This balance is achieved through circular booths crafted from powder-coated metal and made in Portugal, featuring the hotel's sun motif. The use of this distinctive material adds a unique touch to the space. articles.summary: A decline in investor appetite for Bitcoin and other cryptocurrencies is contributing to a downturn in the market.
articles.content: The cryptocurrency market is experiencing a downturn, with Bitcoin falling over 4% to $68,500 on Friday. This decline has erased gains made by Bitcoin over the past three months and raises questions about whether its bear market was ever truly over. According to CryptoQuant, an analytics provider for cryptocurrencies, investor appetite for Bitcoin is weakening. Its demand indicator has not been this low since December 2023, and investors are again selling Bitcoin exchange-traded funds. The crypto market's downturn is not limited to just Bitcoin, as other assets such as Tether's USDT have also seen significant declines. Over the past two months, the total value of USDT has shrunk by $7.7 billion, indicating a decrease in available cash within crypto markets. Economists had underestimated inflation rates, which rose 0.4% in October, and even without considering food and energy prices, inflation ran hotter than forecast. Gold prices plummeted to near $3,900 an ounce on Friday, a significant drop from its January peak of around $5,600. This decline comes despite gold's traditional status as a safe-haven asset during times of economic uncertainty. Bitcoin investors are also feeling the heat as their digital asset continues to slide in value. After reaching a high of $58,000 in June, Bitcoin had shown signs of recovery in August when the U.S. Treasury announced plans to expand its bond buybacks. However, this rally was short-lived, and Bitcoin has since been trending downwards. The recent midterm elections have added to the challenges facing the crypto industry, which has historically relied on Republican allies to advance favorable legislation. Despite this, Bitcoin initially absorbed the news without a significant reaction. According to Stephen Coltman, head of macro at 21Shares, investors had anticipated the outcome of the midterm elections and were not surprised by the results. He noted that while the elections may have changed the regulatory landscape in the long term, they do not alter the current interpretation of regulations. The stability provided by a two-year window without significant regulatory changes has helped Bitcoin to maintain its value thus far, but investors remain cautious as the asset continues to slide. The cryptocurrency market is being pulled in multiple directions as investors seek yield amidst rising inflation. The AI boom is one of the key factors influencing Bitcoin's outlook, drawing attention and investment dollars away from other assets like gold. This trend has created an "AI black hole" that is absorbing funds and leaving some assets, including Bitcoin, struggling to compete. However, this link can also be a liability for Bitcoin as it makes it vulnerable to being dragged down by the sector's performance. When enthusiasm for AI wanes, investors may reassess their portfolios and sell off assets that have underperformed. The AI boom is having a positive effect on the economy, enabling companies to borrow and spend freely. This has helped keep interest rates high, giving the Fed room to maintain its inflation-fighting strategy. The economic strength provided by AI spending could be short-lived if rising borrowing costs force companies to cut back on investments, potentially weakening the economy. The interplay between AI and interest rates may ultimately benefit Bitcoin as it seeks to stabilize in value. As investors become more cautious and reassess their portfolios, they may look for assets that can provide a safe haven from market volatility, giving Bitcoin some much-needed breathing room. The Trump team has been successful in getting these rulings, with many opponents choosing not to appeal or seeking to delay the process. This year, Close will be among those celebrated at the Los Angeles ceremony on Sunday. Her subsequent nominations were also notable, including one for her performance as Sarah Cooper in "The Big Chill". "I never even thought about the possibility of being nominated for an Oscar," Close said, recalling her initial reaction to receiving the news while filming "The Big Chill. articles.summary: After nearly 25 years abroad, Tina Aswani-Omprakash has finally returned to India and is reconnecting with her roots and family.
articles.content: Tina Aswani-Omprakash, a woman living with Crohn's disease, has finally returned to India after nearly 25 years abroad. Her journey was not without its challenges, but it marked an important milestone in her life. The trip allowed Aswani-Omprakash to reconnect with her roots, family, and food she had previously avoided due to her condition. This experience was made possible through careful preparation and the support of her doctors. It's clear that her health journey has been a long and difficult one. Aswani-Omprakash has undergone over 20 surgeries and struggled with debilitating illness for many years. The trip was a testament to her perseverance and determination to live life to the fullest despite her condition. Her experience highlights the impact of travel on our sense of connection to culture. The journey itself involved exploring historic palaces, temples, and meeting relatives for the first time. This blend of cultural immersion and family connections likely played a significant role in Aswani-Omprakash's healing process. It's clear that her trip to India was about more than just sightseeing. As part of her travels, Aswani-Omprakash took a tuk-tuk ride up the Chamundi Hills near Mysuru, India, which lasted around 30 minutes. The experience was significant for her, marking an important moment in her journey towards healing and self-discovery. The symptoms of inflammatory bowel disease can be unpredictable and debilitating, affecting areas far beyond the digestive system. For some individuals, this can lead to a multitude of issues, including joint pain, eye problems, constipation, and gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD). These extraintestinal manifestations often require a multifaceted approach to manage. As a child, I experienced these symptoms firsthand, but at the time, my doctors didn't connect them to an underlying condition. It wasn't until much later that I received a diagnosis of inflammatory bowel disease, specifically, ulcerative colitis, in 2006. The journey to this point was marked by periods of intense discomfort and uncertainty. Traveling with IBD can be particularly challenging due to the unpredictability of flare-ups and the need for constant vigilance. Even short trips or simple activities could become daunting tasks, filled with anxiety about potential complications. This fear often led me to avoid traveling altogether, even when it was something I deeply desired. My experiences with street food in India were especially memorable, or rather, unforgettable. A day trip to the Taj Mahal from New Delhi ended with all of us eating at a local market stall. The consequences were swift and severe, leaving me severely ill for weeks afterwards. My health issues had become so debilitating that I was forced to stop working several years ago and live on disability benefits. The thought of my condition eventually killing me seemed like a very real possibility, leaving me feeling lost and uncertain about my future. Over the course of two years, my symptoms worsened dramatically, causing severe bleeding and significant weight loss among other complications. These debilitating symptoms made everyday life a challenge, and I often wondered how much longer I could cope with this level of suffering. On July 4, 2008, I underwent a major surgery to remove my colon, a decision that would later prove to be both liberating and complicated. To minimize health risks, my doctors ordered additional tests, including an intestinal ultrasound, to rule out any complications in my digestive system. They also prescribed antibiotics, steroids, and probiotics as a precautionary measure against potential flare-ups or traveler's diarrhea. When planning our trip, my husband and I booked a hotel that offered a range of amenities, including filtered water and a private bathroom with easy access for overnight trips. Our relatives were not entirely supportive of this decision, but it provided us with the comfort and security we needed during our time in India. To reduce my chances of getting ill, I took precautions by avoiding street vendors and opting for hot foods only. Despite these restrictions, I was still able to enjoy a wide variety of delicious and authentic local cuisine. In Mysuru, we discovered a restaurant called MTR that specialized in South Indian dishes like dosas, which are a particular favorite of mine. The lentil soup often served with dosas can be quite spicy, but the staff is happy to accommodate requests for plain dosas with potatoes instead. This adaptation allowed us to indulge in local flavors while minimizing the risk of triggering an IBD flare-up. It was a small but significant victory to enjoy our time in India without compromising my health. Cultural differences played a significant role in my journey towards diagnosis and treatment. I encountered numerous obstacles that tested my resolve, from navigating unfamiliar medical procedures to confronting deeply ingrained family values. My relatives' experiences during the 1947 partition of India and Pakistan had left an indelible mark on our family's perspective, fueling a deep-seated mistrust of Western medicine. This skepticism was particularly pronounced in my own family, who had lost trust in the West due to past traumas. As a result, they were extremely hesitant about seeking medical attention or undergoing surgery. Their concerns not only affected my well-being but also had far-reaching implications for our community's values and traditions. The pressure to conform to societal expectations weighed heavily on me, particularly regarding marriageability and family reputation. My family history of Crohn's disease and colorectal cancer added an extra layer of complexity to my situation. My father's untimely passing from these conditions when I was just eight years old left a lasting impact on our family. Despite this inheritance, I had to fight for the medical attention I needed, advocating tirelessly for myself until I finally received the colonoscopy that would provide me with answers and treatment options. As I navigated this challenging period, I began to realize that fear is not an insurmountable obstacle but rather a mindset that can be overcome. By acknowledging and confronting my fears, I was able to tap into a reservoir of inner strength and resilience that enabled me to push through even the most daunting challenges. Traveling to India for treatment required a tremendous amount of courage and determination, especially considering the unfamiliar foods and surroundings that threatened to trigger my condition. Yet, it was precisely this journey that allowed me to reclaim control over my life and find peace with my diagnosis, ultimately transforming my relationship with my health and well-being. This may involve offering a wider range of unique destinations from LAX, in order to differentiate itself from competitors like Delta and United. American's decision to bolster its presence at LAX reflects the airport's status as one of the nation's most competitive hubs, with each of the major legacy carriers operating a significant hub there. articles.title: NFL Teams Experience Unpredictable Week 10
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders stunned the NFC East-leading New York Giants in a thrilling upset victory, with multiple passing touchdowns and interceptions within an 8-minute window.
articles.content: The NFL's Week 10 kicked off with an unprecedented display of unpredictability, as the Washington Commanders stunned the NFC East-leading New York Giants in a thrilling upset victory. In a wild final stretch, the game saw two passing touchdowns and three interceptions, all within an 8-minute and 25-second window. This marked the first time in 25 years that a game featured multiple passing touchdowns and at least three interceptions in its last 10 minutes, dating back to Week 16 of the 2001 season between the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals. Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels engineered an incredible comeback with a go-ahead touchdown pass from 32 yards out to Stefon Diggs just 57 seconds before time's up. The game ultimately came down to Washington cornerback Rasul Dougal's crucial interception with only 25 seconds remaining on the clock, securing the win for his team. The Week 10 slate promises more dramatic turns of events as the league's top contenders face off in pivotal matchups. One such showdown takes place on Sunday Night Football, where first-place Pittsburgh Steelers clash with the Cincinnati Bengals in a battle for AFC North supremacy. Joe Burrow's high-powered offense has been driving the Bengals' success, boasting an impressive average of 30 points per game, second only to another team in the league. Meanwhile, Pittsburgh relies on edge rusher T.J. Watt and a stingy defense that allows just 18.0 points per game, ranking them fourth-best in this category. The Steelers-Bengals showdown is expected to be an intense affair, with both teams vying for control of their division. The outcome will undoubtedly have significant implications for the rest of the season, as these two top teams battle it out for dominance in the AFC North. The Steelers' stinginess on defense is a notable aspect of their season so far, having allowed just 12 total touchdowns in eight games. This statistic puts them tied for second-fewest touchdowns allowed in the league this year, and they trail only the Minnesota Vikings by one touchdown. The Vikings have allowed a total of 11 touchdowns this season. Joe Burrow's upcoming game against the Steelers will be a challenging one, as he attempts to join an elite group of quarterbacks in NFL history. By achieving at least four total touchdowns on Sunday night, he would match Peyton Manning's feat from 2004 and become just the second quarterback with four-plus total touchdowns in five consecutive games. The Steelers' defense has been effective in limiting their opponents' scoring opportunities this season. However, Burrow is currently on a hot streak, having thrown for at least four touchdowns in each of his last four games. His ability to stay focused under pressure will be crucial if he's to overcome the Steelers' formidable defense. When these two teams met earlier in the season, the Steelers emerged victorious after Burrow fumbled with just 53 seconds left on the clock. Despite this setback, Burrow still managed an impressive performance, completing 28 of 37 passes for 282 yards and three touchdowns. The Jacksonville Jaguars' stingy defense has been a major factor in their success this season, ranking second in the league in points allowed per game. However, that unit will be put to the test on Sunday when it faces off against Tony Pollard and the Tennessee Titans. Pollard's impressive performance last week has him riding high, with 129 yards rushing and three touchdowns against the Cleveland Browns. In a remarkable feat, Pollard became just the fourth player in Titans history to achieve this level of success in consecutive games, joining Derrick Henry, Chris Johnson, and Pro Football Hall of Famer Earl Campbell as members of this exclusive club. Pollard's pursuit of one last payday in the 2027 offseason is likely driving his motivation, and it will be intriguing to see how he fares against the revamped Jaguars defense, which has undergone significant changes ahead of the trade deadline. The Minnesota Vikings' season is gaining momentum after securing Kirk Cousins' return from the Las Vegas Raiders in a trade that cost them a third-round pick. This move is expected to boost their offense, which has been struggling despite having one of the league's best defenses. The tandem of Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz has managed only 12 offensive touchdowns this season, a number tied for the fewest by a team with a 6-2 or better start since 1950. Cousins' addition is likely to make a significant impact on the Vikings' offense, as he brings an impressive track record of 20 passing touchdowns, second-most in the NFL. However, his return may not be straightforward, especially given the challenge posed by the Green Bay Packers, who have been aggressive in taking away the ball this season. The Packers have accumulated the second-most takeaways and interceptions in the league, with a notable contribution from safety Xavier McKinney, who co-leads the league with five interceptions. His teammate Evan Williams has also made a significant impact, with three interceptions tied for seventh-most in the NFL. McKinney and Williams will be a formidable combination for Cousins to face, particularly on Sunday at Lambeau Field. The Packers' ability to take away the ball will put Cousins under pressure, making it difficult for him to establish a rhythm with his teammates. Cousins' connection with Justin Jefferson is one of the most potent in the league, averaging 98.9 passing yards per game over their shared games together. However, this pairing may not be enough to overcome the Packers' defense and its ability to take away the ball, which could lead to a tough outing for Cousins at Lambeau Field. The Atlanta Falcons' Bijan Robinson has been making his mark on the league this season, and it's hard to argue against his worth given his impressive numbers. With 880 rushing yards before Week 10, he was leading the pack in that department. However, Robinson is about to face a formidable opponent in the Kansas City Chiefs defense. This unit has been stingy, allowing just 17.9 points per game and only 12 touchdowns all season. They're also near the bottom of the league when it comes to giving up rushing yards, with an average of 97.5 yards allowed per game. Despite these tough stats, Robinson is expected to have a big day on the ground against the Chiefs. With his quarterback struggling, Atlanta will likely hand him the ball over 20 times - a feat he's only achieved three times this season so far. The Falcons' decision to rely heavily on Robinson should pay off, as he wears down the Chiefs defense with each carry. In other news, Cleveland Browns quarterback Deshaun Watson has been sacked more than any other player in the league this season. With 33 sacks under his belt, Watson will face an even tougher challenge when he takes on the Houston Texans and their All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. Anderson's impressive numbers include a league-leading 9.5 sacks through nine weeks, making him a major threat to Watson's ability to throw quickly. Watson plans to quickly distribute the ball to his rookie wide receivers, KC Concepcion and Benzel Boston, as he aims to limit Anderson's sack opportunities. This strategy will force Watson to throw quickly, increasing the chances of connecting with his receivers. The Texans expect to limit their sacks of Watson to two or fewer on Sunday, despite what may appear to be a challenging situation for him. articles.title: Couples Can Divide Household Chores Without Fighting
articles.summary: By having open conversations about domestic duties, couples can divide responsibilities without tension.
articles.content: Couples are often at odds over household chores, but according to Mel Robbins, there's a way to divide responsibilities without fighting. In her latest podcast appearance, Robbins spoke with Elspeth Velten, editor in chief of Good Housekeeping, about the importance of having open conversations between partners about domestic duties. She notes that many couples fail to discuss these issues directly, leading to an uneven distribution of tasks and resentment building up over time. When household chores become a source of tension, it's essential to address them before emotions run high, as Robbins points out, there's no need to be in the midst of a frustrating situation to bring up the issue. Making a "friction list is another way to tackle household chores without conflict. This technique involves identifying tasks that one partner particularly dislikes, and addressing them as potential sources of tension before they escalate into full-blown arguments. Tasks like unloading the dishwasher or folding laundry may seem mundane, but for some people, they can be a source of significant frustration. By acknowledging these friction points" and discussing them openly with their partner, couples can work together to find solutions that suit everyone's needs. Some individuals may have been conditioned by upbringing or societal expectations not to take on certain household responsibilities, such as cooking or cleaning. This lack of training or expectation can lead to resentment and conflict in relationships when these tasks are left unaddressed. Dividing household chores can be a contentious issue in relationships when one partner consistently leaves tasks undone, leading to resentment and conflict. This lack of training or expectation can create tension in partnerships, making it essential for couples to establish clear responsibilities. It's possible that both partners may be contributing to the problem, with some research suggesting that girls are not immune to overparenting either, which can lead to difficulties in managing household tasks independently. By extending grace and understanding to each other, couples may be able to address friction points more effectively, leading to a smoother division of labor. articles.title: Why does El Salvador's Bukele have troops in Haiti?

articles.title: Deployment of Salvadoran Troops in Haiti Sparks Concerns Over Legitimacy
articles.summary: A joint task force between El Salvador and Haiti has successfully targeted the headquarters of two gangs, according to reports.
articles.content: Reports are emerging of a significant development in Haiti's ongoing crisis, where the country has been plagued by protests, presidential assassination, and gang violence since 2018. Haiti's Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aime recently praised a major breakthrough in combating gang violence, crediting the involvement of Salvadoran forces with "the commitment of the Salvadorean forces in the fight against gangs." El Salvador President Nayib Bukele had earlier stated that a joint task force between the countries had successfully targeted what he described as "the house of Lanmo San Jou and the 400 Mawozo gang's headquarters." He also shared an unverified video on social media showing helicopters firing at a sprawling property. The deployment of Salvadoran troops in Haiti, nearly 2,000 kilometers from their home country, began at the start of 2025. The deployment of Salvadoran troops in Haiti has sparked concerns about the legitimacy of their presence. Haiti's Fils-Aime has publicly expressed gratitude to the Salvadorean military for contributing to the fight against gangs, stating that they are working alongside the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force (GSF) to regain control of territory and restore state authority. The GSF has been operating in Haiti since 2016, but experts question whether El Salvador's involvement is a legitimate effort or an attempt to exert influence over the country. Jake Johnston, a Haiti expert at the Center for Economic and Policy Research, notes that there are concerns about coordination between different security forces and entities involved in the operation. He suggests that El Salvador may be trying to frame its actions as independent decisions rather than part of a larger effort. A recent UN report highlights the severity of violence in Haiti, describing bloody turf wars, sexual violence, and other abuses committed by security forces against gangs, often with the support of private military companies using drones. The deployment of El Salvadoran troops to Haiti has raised eyebrows among observers who see a pattern emerging in President Nayib Bukele's foreign policy. His government's tough stance on gang violence at home, known as "mano dura, seems to be inspiring similar tactics abroad. According to Romain Le Cour Grandmaison, an expert from the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime, Haiti's gang problem is far more complex than El Salvador's. The country's prisons were emptied in 2024, leaving no space for new inmates, and its justice system has effectively ground to a halt. As a result, Haiti's criminal groups have taken on a life of their own. These groups are not your average gangs, but rather well-organized militias with control over territory, taxation systems, access to weapons of war, and even political networks that protect them from prosecution. Experts warn that importing El Salvador's approach may not yield the same results in Haiti. Despite being once labeled a shithole country" by US President Donald Trump, relations between the US and El Salvador have improved significantly during his second term in office. El Salvador's security concerns are being addressed through a unique arrangement between President Nayib Bukele and US President Donald Trump. The increasing number of migrants deported from the US to El Salvador has heightened tensions, rising by 98% at the start of this year, according to Le Cour Grandmaison. This shift in dynamics has given Bukele more leeway to prioritize his country's security needs, thanks to the backing he has received from Trump. The relationship between the two leaders has been a game-changer for El Salvador, allowing it to operate with greater autonomy in matters of national security. Trump's words on Haiti reflect the complexities of regional politics and the delicate balance of power in the area. articles.summary: As a busy mom in my 40s, I've come to expect a lot from my foundation - it has to cover up acne scars, hyperpigmentation, and redness while also addressing dry skin that makes blending...
articles.content: As a busy mom in my 40s, I've come to expect a lot from my foundation - it has to cover up acne scars, hyperpigmentation, and redness while also addressing dry skin that makes blending makeup a challenge. My skin's unique needs can be difficult to meet with traditional foundations, which often settle into fine lines, emphasize pores, and dull the complexion. With limited time to devote to my beauty routine, I need a product that can multitask and deliver real results. Fortunately, L'Oréal Paris True Match Hyaluron Tinted Balm Foundation has exceeded my expectations - its formula is comprised of 80 percent skincare ingredients, including hyaluronic acid, which helps hydrate and smooth skin while reducing the appearance of fine lines and wrinkles over time. Applying the L'Oréal Paris True Match Hyaluron Tinted Balm Foundation was a straightforward process thanks to the teardrop-shaped sponge applicator that came with it. I applied the foundation from the center of my face outward, using long strokes to blend it into my skin. The foundation's unique luminous texture was immediately noticeable - it had a subtle sheen that caught the light without looking too shiny or artificial. As I worked the product into my skin, I found that it sank in effortlessly and provided a smooth, even base for the rest of my makeup. The compact packaging is also a convenient feature, as it allows for easy touch-ups on-the-go - no more digging through a cluttered makeup bag or rummaging around for a separate foundation bottle. As I navigated the unpredictable coastal weather of Maine, my foundation remained intact even after hours in front of my laptop. I didn't need to worry about touching up my makeup during a quick break at the gym, thanks to the compact packaging that made reapplying easy and convenient. The foundation's ability to withstand the challenges of a busy day was put to the test when I had to leave for back-to-back high school soccer games, where I could have easily found myself in a situation where my skin would be exposed to harsh weather conditions. I was impressed that after a long day, including hours at my laptop and time spent outdoors, my foundation still looked fresh and my skin felt hydrated. The product's performance was particularly noteworthy given the time of day when foundation can start to look tired on mature skin. A quick face check before showering revealed that my foundation had not settled into my crow’s feet, and my skin remained comfortable and well-moisturized. The foundation provided a comfortable base throughout the day, allowing me to maintain my natural look without feeling weighed down by heavy makeup. For those seeking a hydrating foundation that caters to mature skin, I'd suggest exploring products that incorporate hyaluronic acid and other nourishing ingredients, ensuring both hydration and smooth application.
